metadata.case_name: PUK CHUNG YU v. LAM SHUI KEUNG AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: second degree burn over his right neck and back regions.
source: the plaintiff was immediately sent to the A&E of CMC where he was found to have second degree burn over his right neck and back regions.

injuries.description: Right lateral thigh: A skin graft donor area scar was readily noticeable, measuring 14 cm x 4 cm. The scar was pale, flat but with a thickened coarse texture. There is a noticeable raised thickened posterior margin along 1 cm of the scar. Although the scar can be concealed by clothing, it will be evident when the plaintiff wears swimsuit or above-knee shorts. The scar cannot be surgically improved.
source:
(a) Right lateral thigh: A skin graft donor area scar was readily
noticeable, measuring 14 cm x 4 cm. The scar was pale, flat but with a
thickened coarse texture. There is a noticeable raised thickened posterior
margin along 1 cm of the scar. Although the scar can be concealed by clothing,
it will be evident when the plaintiff wears swimsuit or above-knee shorts. The
scar cannot be surgically improved.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the hip or thigh

injuries.description: Upper neck: A scar was readily noticeable at the right upper posterior aspect, measuring 4 cm x 2 cm. The lower 0.5 cm of the margin was raised and thickened. This will always be noticeable and can only be partially concealed by clothing.
source:
(b) Upper neck: A scar was readily noticeable at the right upper posterior
aspect, measuring 4 cm x 2 cm. The lower 0.5 cm of the margin was raised and
thickened. This will always be noticeable and can only be partially concealed
by clothing.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of neck

injuries.description: Lower neck: Another scar was readily noticeable at right lower part adjacent to shoulder region, measuring 6.5 cm x 3.5 cm. The scar is soft and pliable with a slight coarse texture. This will always be noticeable and can only be partially concealed by clothing.
injuries.body_part: right lower neck adjacent to shoulder region
source:
(c) Lower neck: Another scar was readily noticeable at right lower part
adjacent to shoulder region, measuring 6.5 cm x 3.5 cm. The scar is soft and
pliable with a slight coarse texture. This will always be noticeable and can
only be partially concealed by clothing.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of neck

injuries.description: Occipital area: A noticeable bald patch scar can be seen at the lower occipital scalp, measuring 1.4 cm x 1 cm. The scar is partially concealed by hair. There was also a raised hairline at the occipital hair margin of about 2 cm. These can be surgically restored by a more complex procedure when the plaintiff grows older.
source:
(d) Occipital area: A noticeable bald patch scar can be seen at the lower
occipital scalp, measuring 1.4 cm x 1 cm. The scar is partially concealed by
hair. There was also a raised hairline at the occipital hair margin of about 2
cm. These can be surgically restored by a more complex procedure when the
plaintiff grows older.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of scalp

injuries.description: There was also a small stitch sinus measuring 1 cm x 0.5 cm with retained debris and possible stitch remnant on the margin of the scar area, but this can be surgically removed.

the plaintiff after the Accident cried every night
plaintiff had to put on pressure garment, from head to toe, for a considerable period which no doubt caused a lot of discomfort to the plaintiff
limited walking endurance and frequent fall during walking

treatments_received: sent to the A&E of Caritas Medical Centre and treated for second degree burn
operation for debridement and skin grafting on 10 January 2007 with a graft taken from the plaintiff’s right lateral thigh
occupational therapy for scar management (application of silicone gel, pressure therapy and massage of aqueous cream)
physiotherapy for motor training starting 22 January 2009
treatments_future: removal/restoration of the bald patch at occipital scalp (more complex procedure when older)

losses.description: Permanent cosmetic injuries and residual scars affecting appearance, partial concealment by clothing or hair, and associated discomfort from scar management treatments.
